direction: April attends to small forms of nourishment and renewal: remembered plums, grass at a rain-filled hoofprint, and cotton wicks prepared for humble lamps. Warm pastel fruit, close earthy watercolor and spare charcoal vary density and material. Exploitation, the identified beloved and the long ecological-spiritual argument remain text-led. The existing archived metadata-only poem385 is preserved and receives no new assignment.

items.title: Pullum on the cloth
items.rationale: The speaker remembers the local name, taste and small evidence of eating plums. Fruit beside a juice mark preserves the playful private appetite and domestic memory without inventing the speaker or a market documentary.

review.notes: Pass at normal size: three uneven plums overlap naturally, restrained bloom and split skin give a plausible source for juice absorbed into a cloth fold. Warm painterly marks and quiet right side preserve playful appetite and memory. Close scale is stronger than requested but no advertisement props, invented person or lettering.

items.alt: Three red-purple plums rest on cotton beside a small juice stain.

items.title: Green in a small imprint
items.rationale: The ending imagines tireless renewal through a tuft of grass in water held by a hoofprint. Keep that small scale and precarious life instead of illustrating the poem’s many deities and sacrificial images.

review.notes: Pass at normal size: two softened adjoining hoof depressions hold water below damp soil edges, grass roots meet the margin, restrained reflection and uneven blades support small renewal. The imprint is a poetic ground study rather than a species-identification diagram; no animal, miracle glow or illustrative deity.

items.alt: A few green grass blades grow beside water held in a shallow cloven hoofprint.

items.title: Cotton wicks for small lamps
items.rationale: The tribute finds sacred generosity in humble daily acts and describes rolling cotton wicks. A small unfinished task suggests that care without fabricating a likeness of Sai of Shirdi or an authoritative shrine.

review.notes: Pass at normal size: simple clay diya has a coherent rim and stable floor contact; one wick lies along its lip while two unequal rolled pieces remain beside raw cotton. Sparse charcoal and terracotta keep the practical unfinished task central. No flame, iconography or invented Sai likeness; second lamp naturally cropped.

items.alt: Cotton and hand-rolled wicks lie beside simple unlit earthen lamps.

text_led.rationale: The account of empires built on exploited bodies should speak directly; avoid fabricated remains or theatrical suffering.
The beloved is specifically described in a framed image. Without an identified photograph, preserve the poem as text rather than invent a face or substitute an empty frame.
The long ecological and spiritual argument connects many traditions. Keep it text-led rather than inventing sacred imagery or flattening its progression into a collage.
